name.en: NEET-UG Registration (National Eligibility cum Entrance Test for Undergraduate)

description.en: NEET-UG (National Eligibility cum Entrance Test for Undergraduate) is the single national-level entrance examination for admission to MBBS, BDS, BAMS, BSMS, BUMS, BHMS, and other undergraduate medical and dental courses in India. Conducted by the National Testing Agency (NTA), NEET-UG is mandatory for admission to all medical institutions including government, private, deemed, and central universities. The examination is conducted annually in pen-and-paper (OMR-based) mode across multiple cities in India and abroad.

verifiedConditions.appliesTo: Indian citizens, NRIs, OCIs, PIOs, and foreign nationals as per NTA eligibility norms
verifiedConditions.claim: Indian citizens, Non-Resident Indians (NRIs), Overseas Citizens of India (OCIs), Persons of Indian Origin (PIOs), and foreign nationals are eligible to apply for NEET-UG subject to fulfilling other eligibility criteria.

verifiedConditions.appliesTo: All applicants — must have completed 17 years of age at the time of admission or as specified in the notification
verifiedConditions.claim: The candidate must have completed 17 years of age at the time of admission or will complete 17 years on or before 31st December of the year of admission.

verifiedConditions.appliesTo: All applicants — must have passed Class 12 with Physics, Chemistry, and Biology/Biotechnology
verifiedConditions.claim: The candidate must have passed Class 12 or equivalent examination with Physics, Chemistry, Biology/Biotechnology, and English as core subjects from a recognized board. Candidates appearing in Class 12 examination in the current year are also eligible to apply.

unverifiedEligibility: The upper age limit for NEET-UG has been subject to court rulings and may vary by notification year.
Minimum aggregate percentage in qualifying subjects (50% for General, 40% for OBC/SC/ST, 45% for PwD) may be revised.
Number of attempts permitted may be limited or unlimited depending on the current year's notification.

requirements.claim: Valid Aadhaar card number for Indian citizens. Foreign nationals and candidates from Jammu & Kashmir, Meghalaya, and Assam may use alternative valid identity documents such as passport, ration card, or bank account details.
Recent passport-sized photograph (white background, 10 KB to 200 KB, JPG/JPEG format) and scanned signature (4 KB to 30 KB, JPG/JPEG format) as per NTA specifications.
Class 10 passing certificate or birth certificate as proof of date of birth. The date of birth recorded in the Class 10 certificate is taken as final.
Class 12 marksheet or equivalent for candidates who have already passed. Candidates appearing in Class 12 in the current year submit their marksheet at the time of counselling.

Category certificate (SC/ST/OBC-NCL) issued by the competent authority in the prescribed format for candidates claiming reservation benefits. PwD certificate from a Government medical board if applicable.
Valid email address and active mobile number for receiving OTP, application confirmation, admit card notifications, and result updates from NTA.

processInformation.claim: Register on the NEET-UG portal (neet.nta.nic.in) by providing name, email, mobile number, and date of birth. An application number and password are generated upon successful registration.

Fill the online application form with personal details, academic qualifications, choice of exam cities (up to four preferences), and category/reservation details. Upload scanned photograph, signature, and required documents as per NTA specifications.

Pay the examination fee online through debit card, credit card, net banking, or UPI. The fee varies by category: General — Rs. 1,700, General-EWS/OBC-NCL — Rs. 1,600, SC/ST/PwD/Third Gender — Rs. 1,000. An additional GST of 18% is applicable. The fee is non-refundable.

Download the admit card from the NEET-UG portal approximately 15-20 days before the examination date. The admit card contains the candidate's examination centre details, roll number, photograph, and instructions. It must be carried to the examination centre along with a valid photo ID.

output.claim: Upon completion of the examination and declaration of results, qualified candidates receive a NEET-UG scorecard containing their total marks, percentile, All India Rank (AIR), and category rank. The scorecard is valid for admission to MBBS, BDS, BAMS, BSMS, BUMS, BHMS, and other undergraduate medical courses through centralised (AIQ) and state-level counselling conducted by MCC and respective state authorities.

fees.applicability: Examination fee for General/Unreserved category candidates
fees.claim: The examination fee for General category candidates is Rs. 1,700 plus 18% GST (total approximately Rs. 2,006). For General-EWS/OBC-NCL candidates, the fee is Rs. 1,600 plus GST. For SC/ST/PwD/Third Gender candidates, the fee is Rs. 1,000 plus GST. Indian candidates from abroad pay Rs. 9,500 plus GST. The fee is payable online and is non-refundable.

fees.applicability: Examination fee for SC/ST/PwD/Third Gender category candidates
fees.claim: Reduced examination fee of Rs. 1,000 plus 18% GST (total approximately Rs. 1,180) for candidates belonging to SC, ST, PwD, and Third Gender categories. Fee concession is applicable upon valid category certificate submission.

processingTime.applicability: Registration window duration from opening to closing of application
processingTime.claim: The NEET-UG registration window is typically open for 30 to 45 days. Results are declared within 30-45 days after the examination. The entire cycle from registration to counselling spans approximately 4-6 months. Admit cards are released approximately 15-20 days before the examination date.

sources.title: NEET-UG Official Portal — National Testing Agency
sources.publisher: National Testing Agency, Ministry of Education, Government of India
sources.evidenceExcerpt: The NEET-UG official portal provides registration, application form submission, admit card download, answer key challenge, and result declaration for the National Eligibility cum Entrance Test for undergraduate medical admissions. The portal publishes the official information bulletin with detailed eligibility criteria, fee structure, exam pattern, and syllabus.
claimsSupported: NEET-UG is mandatory for admission to all UG medical courses in India.
Examination fee is Rs. 1,700 for General, Rs. 1,600 for OBC-NCL/EWS, Rs. 1,000 for SC/ST/PwD.
Candidates must be 17 years old at the time of admission.
Class 12 with Physics, Chemistry, and Biology is mandatory.
Admit card is released 15-20 days before examination.
sources.uncertainty: Fee structure, age limits, and number of attempts may change with each year's notification.

sources.title: National Testing Agency — Official Website
sources.publisher: National Testing Agency, Ministry of Education, Government of India
sources.evidenceExcerpt: NTA is the autonomous body responsible for conducting NEET-UG along with other national entrance examinations. The NTA website provides general information about examination schedules, grievance redressal, and policy updates applicable to all NTA-conducted examinations.
claimsSupported: NTA conducts NEET-UG annually as a pen-and-paper examination.
Category certificates must be in prescribed format from competent authority.
Results include AIR, percentile, and category rank.
Counselling is conducted by MCC for AIQ seats and by state authorities for state quota.
sources.uncertainty: Examination mode (pen-and-paper vs. CBT) and frequency may change based on Government policy decisions.

limitations: The examination pattern, syllabus, and fee structure are subject to change with each year's official notification.
This record covers the registration process only and does not detail the counselling or admission process.
Upper age limit and number of permitted attempts may vary by notification year and are subject to court orders.
Category-specific reservation percentages and eligibility criteria are governed by respective counselling authorities.
The record does not cover state-level NEET counselling processes or institutional-specific admission requirements.
NTA may introduce changes to the examination mode (pen-and-paper or computer-based) in future years.
